name: LANKO 145 Floor Leveller
paste:
LANKO® 145 FLOOR LEVELLER: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller, September 2024, Version 01.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/y/lanko-145-floor-leveller.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2024, Version 01.01).
1.2 Product description.
    - LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller is an economical flooring leveller underlayment designed for high build applications from 3-75mm in a single pour.
    - LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller is suitable for single bag mixing, multi bag mixing and pump machine applications.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Recommended underlayment for all commercial; & residential floor coverings.
    - Levelling of uneven concrete from 3mm up to 75mm thickness.
    - Suitable for new or old internal concrete substrates.
    - Can be used in conbination with Davco and Lanko ranges of installation materials.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: AN ECONOMICAL HIGH BUILD LEVELLING & SMOOTHING COMPOUND FOR INTERNAL USE
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (September 2024, Version 01.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Very Low VOC (~1 gram per litre)
    - Non-combustible
    - High strength
    - Economical levelling solution
    - Simply mix & apply - No slaking or re-mixing required
    - Good pot life and working time - slow setting
    - Pump or manual application
    - Application build 3mm-75mm in a single pour
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Colour: Grey powder
    - Volatile organic compound (VOC) content: 1 gram per Litre
2.5 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Compressive Strength: 1 day cure – 14MPa to 16 MPa 28 day cure – 25MPa to 30MPa
    - Tensile strength: 28 day cure > 5 MPa
    - Water absorption: Porous
2.6 System structure.
    | Porous Concrete | Non-porous substrate |
    | Lanko® 124 Ultraprime | SikaFloor-14 Prep n Prime |
    | Lanko® 145 Floor Leveller | Lanko® 145 Floor Leveller |
    | Subsequent suitable materials | Subsequent suitable materials |
    | For high moisture (RH) in concrete, Sika® Moisture Barrier System may be considered; |
    | 1. Sikafloor®-158 W Fast Barrier |
    | 2. Sikafloor®-14 Prep N Prime |
    | 3. LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller |
    | Contact your local Sika® office for further information. |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.7 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 20kg Paper bags
    - Shelf life: Unopened bags can be stored for up to 12 months in a cool, dry and weatherproof environment.
    - Storage conditions: Bags must be stored off the floor in dry cool conditions out of direct sunlight. Avoid sitting bags in direct sunlight prior to application.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2024, Version 01.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - Concrete floors should be fully cured, structurally sound, with a minimum pull off strength of 1.5 MPa, clean, dry, and free of surface contaminates and dust for Eg. Concrete must be porous and accept water penetration. Test by lightly sprinkling water on various areas of the substrate. If water penetrates, then a good bond with a selected primer can be achieved. If water beads and fails to be absorbed by the concrete surface contaminants are present then loss of adhesion may occur. Contaminates that are present should be mechanically removed before installation. Concrete must be free of efflorescence and not subject to hydrostatic pressure. If the concrete substrate has efflorescence or high moisture (RH) Sikafloor® moisture barrier system may be considered (Sikafloor®-158 W Fast Barrier + Sikafloor® Prep 'N' Prime + LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller.
    - Contact your local Sika® office for further information.
3.3 Priming - Porous Priming.
    - Lanko® 124 Ultraprime applied neat (undiluted) to surfaces that are to be levelled.
    - Note: Correct amount of priming liquid should always be applied to the prepared substrate giving good penetration and film build.
    - Thin applications may result in pinholing or debonding levelling compound from the substrate.
    - Do Not Allow primer to pool while drying.
    - On particularly porous (mechanically prepared) surfaces or where the initial prime coat absorbs immediately a second coat is recommended. Average dry time ~20–30 min (per coat) When applying exterior under hot, windy conditions (Temperatures above 30ºC), it is essential to wet down any concrete surfaces with clean water prior to priming, so the primer does not flash dry. After wetting down the floor, do not allow the water to pool or pond on the surface. The substrate should appear matt, with no signs of glistening pools evident prior to application of the Lanko® 124 Ultraprime.
    - Non-porous priming
    - Sikafloor®-14 Prep N Prime – undiluted (Neat)
    - Note: When applying primer to Non-porous surface use a paint roller and apply one thin even coat. Sikafloor ®-14 Prep N Prime Must Be Completely Dry (50-60 min+) prior to applying Lanko® products. Chosen primer should completely dry prior to the application of Lanko® Levelling Systems. > Chosen primer should completely dry prior to the application of Lanko® Levelling Systems. > For further detailed information (Product Data Sheet) regarding chosen primer please go to sika.com.au or contact Sika® Australia 1300 22 33 48.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2024, Version 01.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Yield: 12 L = 4m² at 3mm
    - Layer Thickness: 3 - 75mm lifts
    - Mixing Ratio: 3.5 - 3.8 litres of clean cool water per 20kg bag
    - Pot Life: 20 minutes at 23°C & 50% relative humidity.
4.3 Waiting time to overcoating.
    - Allow 24+ hours at 23°C prior to the application of floor coverings.
    - Drying is dependent on thickness of application, temperature, air flow & relative humidity. Increased air flow will help with drying speeds in cooler temperatures.
    Testing moisture content before applying floor coverings is recommended. Note: Freshly applied LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller must be protected from damp, condesation and water while curing for at least 24 hours.
4.4 Mixing.
    - Mix the entire 20kg bag of LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller with 3.5 - 3.8 Litres of clean, cool water.
    - Slowly add powder to the water while mixing thoroughly for 2 minutes to a lumpfree consistency.
    - Not mixing for the recommended time or additional water may result in product irregularities and possible product failure.
4.5 Application. Pour or Pump LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller, then spread with a long handled gauged spreader to heights as required. For touch-ups, use a flat steel trowel. If vinyls are being installed a skim coat of Sikafloor® Level Pro FInish(smoothing compound) may be required. Areas of application must have fresh airflow to assist with product hydration and drying. Closed off rooms with no fresh air will retard the curing process and possibly lead to product failure.
4.6 Application - Second applications.
    - If required, a second coat may be applied as soon as the first coat is firm enough to walk on without causing excessive damage, approximately 2 hours @ 23°C but no later than 4 hours @ 23°C. This installation method is referred to as "wet-on-wet" and higher temperatures/air flow will mean this "wet-onwet" second application time window is reduced, therefore the second coat should always be applied as soon as possible.
    - Note: If the first application is allowed to dry past 4 hours at 23°C, re-priming & subsequent applications should be applied the next day - Normal drying times apply (24+ hours @ 23°C).
4.7 Cleaning of tools. Cleaning of tools and equipment can be done with water prior to the product drying.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not install LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller over particleboard, hardwood floors, parquet floors or metal.
    - Do not mix or apply LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller in temperatures below 10°C and above 35°C and under hot and windy conditions.
    - Keep product cool prior to mixing and do not leave bags in direct sun for extended periods.
    - Protect from hot or strong winds and extremes of temperature for 12hrs after being applied to avoid rapid moisture loss leading to cracking or crazing.
    - All construction/expansion joints in existing concrete must be reflected through Lanko® product as soon as possible to do so.
    - Not recommended as a trafficable surface.
    - Do not use on sloped surfaces that require drainage or in wet areas.
    - Do not use in exterior applications.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient Air Temperature. >10°C - <35°C
5.3 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Do not mix or apply LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller in temperatures below 10°C and above 35°C and under hot and windy conditions.
    - Protect from hot or strong winds and extremes of temperature for 12hrs after being applied to avoid rapid moisture loss leading to cracking or crazing.
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller, September 2024, Version 01.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/y/lanko-145-floor-leveller.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS LANKO® 145 Floor Leveller, version 30/09/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/i/sds-lanko-145-floorleveller.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Lanko 145 SDS, version 09/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/MSDS%20Lanko%20145%20Floor%20Leveller%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
